display_title: fix(cookie): size cookie chunks by their encoded length

head_commit.message:
fix(cookie): size cookie chunks by their encoded length

`setChunkedCookie` split the raw value every `chunkMaxLength` characters,
but each chunk is percent-encoded when serialized: JSON or non-ASCII values
produced chunks well over the ~4KB browser limit, which browsers drop, so
`getChunkedCookie` returned `undefined` on the next request. Slicing by
UTF-16 index could also split a surrogate pair, making `encodeURIComponent`
throw. Split on code points and measure each chunk after encoding.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

display_title: fix(sse): preserve buffered events during overlapping flushes

head_commit.message:
fix(sse): settle unread streams on dispose and drain paused pushes on close

- onDispose: an EventStream whose readable was never consumed (returned
  alongside another value, or body dropped for HEAD) has a backpressured
  first write that never resolves, so close() waited behind it forever and
  onClosed never fired. Cancel the unread side instead, which rejects the
  pending write and settles writer.closed like a client disconnect.
- close(): a paused push landing while the final flush waits on
  backpressure was accepted into a fresh buffer and then orphaned. Loop the
  flush until nothing is buffered before queueing writer.close().

display_title: fix(cookie): include partitioned in the distinct-cookie key

head_commit.message:
fix(cookie): include partitioned in the distinct-cookie key

_getDistinctCookieKey() only considers name/domain/path when deciding
whether a setCookie/deleteCookie call replaces an existing queued
Set-Cookie header for the same response. A partitioned (CHIPS) cookie
lives in a separate browser cookie jar from an unpartitioned cookie
with the same name/domain/path, so treating them as the same key is
wrong: whichever call happens last in the response silently drops the
other's header, even though the browser would happily keep both.

Concretely this breaks the common migration path of adding
`partitioned: true` to an existing cookie -- serving both an old
unpartitioned cookie's clearing header and the new partitioned cookie's
set header in one response collapses to just one Set-Cookie, and which
one survives depends on call order rather than intent.

Adds `partitioned` to the key alongside name/domain/path, plus two
regression tests covering both the "must not merge" and "must still
merge" cases.

name: ci
display_title: fix(session): do not persist a session that is only read

head_commit.message:
fix(session): do not persist a session that is only read

`getSession()` created *and* persisted a brand-new empty session whenever the
request carried none, so any read-only caller (auth middleware checking whether
someone is signed in) issued a `Set-Cookie` to every anonymous visitor. The only
opt-out, `cookie: false`, is all-or-nothing: it also stops real writes from
persisting.

A new session is now initialized in memory only and marked with an internal
`kSessionNew` symbol; the first `updateSession()` persists it and clears the
mark. `useSession()` keeps its documented force-init contract by checking the
mark itself, which works whether the session was created by its own
`getSession()` call or by an earlier one in the same request.

This also drops a wasted seal: `updateSession()` falls back to `getSession()`,
which used to persist the empty session before the real write sealed it again,
so starting a session cost two PBKDF2 seals (4 `deriveBits` calls) instead of
one.

Breaking: a session read but never written is no longer persisted, so its `id`
is not stable across requests. Use `useSession()` (unchanged) or write to the
session to start one.

Resolves #1523

head_commit.message:
ci: tighten publish gating and close remaining unpinned installs

Follow-up hardening from a review of this branch.

publish.yml:
- Gate on `head_repository`, `head_branch` and `github.repository` as well as
  `event == 'push'`. `on.workflow_run.branches: [main]` filters the triggering
  run's `head_branch`, which a fork PR chooses, so a fork branch named `main`
  matched it; only the `if:` was load-bearing, and nothing said so.
- Require `head_sha == github.sha`. npm builds its provenance statement from the
  runner's `GITHUB_SHA` — main's tip under `workflow_run` — not from the `ref:`
  being checked out, so publishing a non-tip commit would attest a commit that
  was never built. It also stops a re-run of an old `ci` run from republishing
  stale code as the newest nightly.
- Move `concurrency` onto the job: job-level groups are evaluated after `if:`,
  so skipped runs no longer occupy the group and cannot evict a pending release.
- Add `timeout-minutes`, which the far less critical preview job already had,
  and which the non-cancelling group amplifies.
- `package-manager-cache: false`, per setup-node's own guidance for privileged
  jobs: a poisoned store would execute with the OIDC token live.
- Assert npm >= 11.5.1 instead of installing `npm@latest`. Node 24.6+ bundles
  11.17.0, but 24.0.0 shipped 11.3.0, so the floor is worth stating.

ci.yml:
- Run the preview publish on pull requests only, and drop `continue-on-error`.
  `publish.yml` fires when the whole workflow concludes, so the preview job was
  serialising ahead of every nightly — up to its 10 minute timeout if pkg.pr.new
  hangs — and `continue-on-error` re-masked at run level what 635812c unmasked
  at step level. On `main`, `ci` now means exactly "tests passed".
- Add a concurrency group, cancelling only for pull requests: a cancelled run on
  `main` concludes `cancelled` and would silently skip that commit's nightly.
- Drop `fetch-depth: 0` (pkg-pr-new only runs `git rev-parse HEAD`) and the
  redundant `pnpm build` (`npm pack` runs `prepack`, which builds).
- Pin the coverage file; vitest's default reporters emit no lcov, and a
  discovery miss after the codecov v3 -> v7 jump would be silent.

All three:
- `persist-credentials: false`, so the token is not left in `.git/config` for
  `pnpm install` lifecycle scripts to read. Not in autofix.yml, where the action
  fetches the PR head from origin and needs it.
- Pin corepack, the last unpinned fetch-and-execute, and normalise the four
  copies of the bootstrap that had already drifted.
- Read the Node version from `.nvmrc`, which existed and nothing consumed.

head_commit.message:
fix(rules): only lift a preflight CORS rule for a routable method

`liftPreflightCors` does a second, method-keyed match for the method named in
`access-control-request-method`, and accepted any `/^[A-Za-z]+$/` token. The
header is attacker-controlled, so a preflight naming a method no rule key can
name still keyed a fresh entry in the shared match memo, evicting real traffic's
entries from the 1024-entry FIFO for a lookup that can never lift anything.

Gate on the `HTTP_METHODS` set `parseRouteKey` already uses (now exported), which
bounds lifted lookups to the methods a rule key can actually be scoped to. Memo
pressure from varying paths is unchanged — the key is method plus pathname, and
the pathname was always free.

head_commit.message:
refactor(body-limit): adopt srvx@0.12.3 limitRequestBody

srvx 0.12.3 (h3js/srvx#281) makes `limitRequestBody` preserve ServerRequest
(proxy-wrap, generic `<T extends Request>`, handles clone()), so h3 no longer
needs its own inline proxy + stream limiter. Delete both and delegate the wrap
to `srvx/body-limit`; keep the synchronous fail-fast checks (413 honest oversized
Content-Length, 400 CL+TE smuggling) in `assertBodySize`.

srvx throws its canonical `ERR_BODY_TOO_LARGE` (status 413) rather than an
HTTPError, so map it back to a handled 413 at every consumption boundary:
`isBodyLimitError` re-throws it (readBody/formData, validated json, json-rpc)
instead of masking as 400, and `toResponse` renders a handled 413 instead of an
unhandled 500 (inlined there to keep the helper out of the core bundle). A
handler reading `event.req` directly now sees the ERR_BODY_TOO_LARGE error.

Bundle guardrails nudged for the toResponse check: H3Core 7600->7650 (gzip
3000->3050), defineHandler 6700->6750 (2700->2750), H3 gzip 6950->7000.

Full suite: 1598 passed, lint + typecheck clean.

getRequestProtocol trusted the x-forwarded-proto header by default,

head_commit.message:
fix(proxy): harden header hygiene, abort classification, and opaque responses

Address a second-round review (ISSUES.md):

- Strip incoming request headers nominated by the client's `Connection`
  header (RFC 9110 §7.6.1), and add `proxy-authorization`/`proxy-connection`
  to the default request denylist so proxy credentials aren't leaked upstream.
  Extract a shared `connectionTokens` helper for both directions.
- Classify aborts by the composed signal's reason instead of only
  `error.name === "AbortError"`, so a client disconnect that aborts with a
  raw socket error (e.g. srvx-on-Node `ECONNRESET`) still yields a quiet 499
  rather than a 502.
- Reject unrelayable opaque/error/status-0 fetch responses with a 502 instead
  of surfacing an empty `200 OK` via `HTTPResponse`'s `status || 200`.
- Use own-property checks in `rewriteCookieProperty` so a polluted prototype
  can't inject phantom domain/path rewrite rules (matches `rewritePrefix`).
- `fetchWithEvent`: accept a `duplex` init, default it for streamed external
  bodies, and clarify that external URLs use native fetch without inheriting
  event headers/context.
- Document that `forwardHeaders` is a denylist-bypass (not an exclusive
  allowlist) and that `x-forwarded-proto`/`-host` derive from `event.url`.

head_commit.message:
fix(request): prevent decode:true from reintroducing path separators

`getRouterParams({ decode: true })` applied `decodeURIComponent` on top of
the pathname that `event.ts` already decoded once (via `decodeURI`, which
preserves reserved chars). A second decode could collapse encoded separators
(`%2f`→`/`, `%5c`→`\`, and `%25`-nested forms) into raw separators,
reintroducing `..` traversal that route matching and pathname-based
middleware never saw.

Decoding now skips over encoded path separators, keeping them in their
encoded form while every other escape still decodes normally. Applies to
`getRouterParam` and `getValidatedRouterParams` via delegation.

head_commit.message:
fix: set explicit content-type for Uint8Array responses

When returning a Uint8Array from an h3 handler, the content-type
header was not set. This caused inconsistent behavior across runtimes:

- Node.js: no content-type set (browsers default to text/html)
- Bun: automatically sets application/octet-stream, triggering file
  download in browsers

The fix explicitly sets content-type: application/octet-stream for
Uint8Array responses when no content-type is already set. This ensures
consistent behavior across runtimes and allows users to override the
content-type by setting it explicitly before returning.

All 1148 functional tests pass. Bundle size tests fail due to the
added bytes (expected for any code addition).

Fixes #1158

display_title: fix: preserve percent-encoded req.url in app event handler

head_commit.message:
fix: preserve percent-encoded `req.url` in app event handler

`createAppEventHandler` was writing the decoded path (from `_decodePath`)
back to `event.node.req.url`. This breaks HTTP proxies (e.g. Nitro dev
server using httpxy) that forward `req.url` directly — they would send
raw UTF-8 bytes instead of percent-encoded form, causing 400 Bad Request
from downstream servers.

Keep a separate `_rawLayerPath` derived from the original encoded URL and
use it for `req.url`, while `event._path` continues using the decoded
form for h3 internal routing and security checks.

Closes h3js/h3#1354

head_commit.message:
fix(security): increase default PBKDF2 iterations from 1 to 600,000

The default PBKDF2 iteration count for session sealing was 1, making
offline brute-force of leaked session tokens trivially fast. OWASP (2023)
recommends at least 600,000 iterations for SHA-1 PBKDF2.

This is a breaking change: existing sealed sessions will fail to unseal
after this update. Users should clear existing sessions or explicitly
set `seal.encryption.iterations` and `seal.integrity.iterations` to 1
in their session config for backward compatibility during migration.

Closes #1313

fix(response): preserve event.res headers (e.g. CORS) on HTTPError

When a handler set headers on event.res (e.g. via handleCors) and then
threw an HTTPError, the error response did not include those headers.
This was because the error handling path returned before the code that
extracts and merges event.res headers.

Now extracts event.res headers in the error path and merges them into
the error response. The onError handler path is unchanged — it can
still access event.res.headers directly.

Closes #1301

was storing the stream in _data without consuming it. This caused
response body and headers to be lost.

Now properly consumes ReadableStream via pipeTo() and writes the
accumulated data to response via res.end().
